clue.text: View from large castle — king's away first

indicators.note: first says this piece leads the answer

parts.note: a team playing away is out, not at home
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: king's reads as king is (away), so the king's letter goes from the castle

parts.note: in chess the castle is the rook
R, for Rex, is the king

explanation.surface: A traveller admires the vista from a great castle while the monarch is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the castle is the rook; R (Rex) is the king. 'first' puts OUT, away, at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a prospect or vista seen from a place.

clue.text: O Little Town, sung to baby ox, ends in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters are in disorder
ends picks the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: A carol, O Little Town of Bethlehem, sung in a stable that ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening O is the definition, the chemical symbol. Last letters E N G O Y X are rearranged ('in trouble').
explanation.definitionFit: O is the chemical symbol for this gaseous element.

clue.text: Makes fun of square relatives

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T
aunts are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone mocks their fuddy-duddy family.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to jeer at them.

clue.text: Musical drama is not funny, it's lots of action

parts.note: an opera is a drama set to music

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A critic complains an opera has no laughs but plenty happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges IS NOT to TIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Military or police actions are operations; the plural gives lots of them.

clue.text: Instrument carried by Jack (a zoologist)

indicators.note: carried by means held within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A scientist named Jack carries a toy instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple humming wind instrument.

clue.text: Messi runs by one, then many — it's shocking!

indicators.note: by places the next piece beside the last
then means the next piece follows on
Messi runs: the footballer's name breaks up and is set out anew

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
C, the Roman hundred, stands for many

explanation.surface: A commentator gasps as Messi dribbles past one defender, then a crowd of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' is the anagram signal; C, the Roman hundred, stands for many.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismic is used figuratively for something earth-shaking, hence startling.

clue.text: Ex-foreign secretary wears small girdle for washing

parts.note: Geoffrey Howe was UK Foreign Secretary in the 1980s
a ring encircles, as a girdle does

explanation.surface: A retired politician dons a tight undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Howe was Thatcher's Foreign Secretary, 1983-89.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathing under a spray of water is a way of washing.

clue.text: Egyptian architect misses pet being around, in my humble opinion

indicators.note: misses means goes without some letters

parts.note: Imhotep designed the step pyramid at Saqqara

indicators.note: being around turns the word pet backwards

explanation.surface: An ancient builder pines for a pet that is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: IMHOTEP drops TEP, which is 'pet' turned 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: A text-speak initialism for the phrase, used online.

clue.text: They produce deft, magic lines when flowing

definitions.text: They produce deft, magic lines when flowing

indicators.note: flowing means the letters are poured into a new order

explanation.surface: The neat curves of iron filings show what these invisible forces draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when flowing' rearranges DEFT MAGIC LINES; the whole clue also describes the answer, whose lines of flux flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions of magnetic force are drawn as flowing lines of flux.

clue.text: Unions, caught in the past, get right with socialist leader

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
once means at some past time

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter

explanation.surface: Trade unions, once nabbed, get right-wing help from a leftist chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert is acting together, so these are agreements or unions.

clue.text: Yankee river for y'all up North?

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and elsewhere in England

explanation.surface: An American asks how 'y'all' would be said in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and others share the name).
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect plural of you, heard in northern England, Ireland and Scotland, just as y'all is in the US South.

clue.text: Chaotic place with heroin injected by heathen meat eater

parts.note: a zoo is slang for a scene of chaos

indicators.note: injected by says the drug's letter goes inside the heathen

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A lurid drugs story: a heathen carnivore shooting up in a chaotic den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected by' puts H inside PAGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoological term for an animal that feeds on other animals, a carnivore.

clue.text: Fielding position gets another 1006 balls?

parts.note: an extra is one more, another
1006 read as 100 and 6: C is the Roman hundred, and six balls make an over in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder is asked to stop yet another thousand-odd deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1006 as 100 (C) then 6 balls (an OVER, six deliveries in cricket). Extra cover is a cricket fielding position on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A named place on a cricket field where a fielder stands.

clue.text: First Lady's bit of 17?

indicators.note: a bit of means only a short stretch from inside the number written out is kept

parts.note: the number is read as a word, spelt out in full as seventeen

explanation.surface: It looks like a cross-reference to clue 17, but the number itself is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is not another clue: write it out as SEVENTEEN and the letters sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam's wife was the first woman, hence a jokey first lady.

clue.text: Between cities and at home, queen wears head garment

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: wears puts the queen inside the garment she has on

parts.note: a turban is wound round the head
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: At home, Her Majesty dons a turban.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen; 'wears' signals she goes inside the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for transport links running from one city to another.

clue.text: I may work with insects a bit, not forgetting ant

definitions.text: I may work with insects a bit, not forgetting ant

indicators.note: may work signals letters being worked into a new order
forgetting means the letters of ant are left out of the pool

explanation.surface: A life scientist muses that their research may involve insects, ants included.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the letters of I, INSECTS A BIT and NOT, with A, N, T removed ('forgetting ant'), are rearranged ('may work').
explanation.definitionFit: A researcher in the life sciences, who might well study insects.

clue.text: Wild animal lives for uncertain times

indicators.note: uncertain means the letters are unsettled

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A beast in the wild lives through precarious days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' rearranges LIVES FOR to SILVERFO.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour variant of the red fox with silvery black fur.

clue.text: Bends over books by lecturer on "European game"

indicators.note: by puts the next piece alongside
on puts the next piece after
over says the word is flipped backwards

parts.note: arcs are curves or bends
B is book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: A teacher stoops over a pile of books on a Continental pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the bends round; 'European game' looks like one phrase but European only gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game of building words from letter tiles.

clue.text: Magnificent men on board said to make wine

parts.note: grand means magnificent

indicators.note: said says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a crew is the people aboard a ship

explanation.surface: Sailors are reputed to brew a splendid drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CRU sounds like CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-ranked French vineyard, and the fine wine from it.

clue.text: Records of English schooling or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Reports on English education, private or not.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus SCHOOLING OR is rearranged ('otherwise').
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: lists of events in time order are records.

clue.text: See 7
Cartoon dog, Spot, catches new balls

indicators.note: catches means holds other letters inside

parts.note: to spot is to spy
O is ball-shaped, so OO is balls

explanation.surface: A cartoon pup called Spot catches fresh tennis balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' signals the new balls going inside the word for spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Brown's beagle in Peanuts.

clue.text: Mother undressed girl

indicators.note: undressed strips off the outer layers, the first and last letters

parts.note: a nanny looks after children like a mother

explanation.surface: A mother takes off a little girl's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: NANNY loses its outside letters ('undressed').
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Rising, minister's answer: "No start to synod?"

parts.note: Rev, the Reverend, is a minister

indicators.note: No says a letter is missing from the answer

parts.note: a solution is an answer

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of synod

explanation.surface: A cleric asks whether a church assembly can do without its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLUTION loses S, the first letter of 'synod' ('No start to').
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising, a revolt against rulers.

clue.text: Head of Ofsted lied about being drunk

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter
about means the letters are turned around in any order

explanation.surface: A school inspector's chief fibs about being intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Ofsted is England's schools inspectorate. 'about' rearranges LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: well oiled means drunk.

clue.text: Material girl

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a twilled cotton cloth used for workwear, and a common female first name.

clue.text: Quantity of money left out to grip Trump's soul

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, money

indicators.note: to grip says one piece holds another inside it
out means the word left is jumbled
soul is the heart, the central letter of the name

explanation.surface: Political gossip about cash being withheld to keep a grip on Trump's inner self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LEFT to ETFL; 'to grip' puts U, the middle ('soul') of TRUMP, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pailful, a measure of amount.

clue.text: A hobbit's sword

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: Tolkien's Baggins, the hobbit of The Hobbit, and an old word for a fine Spanish sword named after Bilbao.

clue.text: Horse's tail pulled by bull in spring and autumn?

indicators.note: by places one piece beside the other
tail pulled removes the last letter

parts.note: equine means of a horse
an ox is a bovine animal like a bull

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene where a bull tugs a horse's tail through the seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail pulled' drops the last letter. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An equinox falls in each of these seasons, around 20 March and 22 September.

clue.text: Ruling family is extremely dirty and filthy

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: nasty means filthy

explanation.surface: A royal house is described as thoroughly grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of hereditary rulers, a ruling house.
